title: Non-inferiority analysis of a risk-stratified prescription reconciliation in the context of the decentralized Unit-Dose administration system
summary:
The medication process in hospitals is complex and carries the risk of errors that can compromise patient safety. Pharmaceutical care can help identify and prevent problems with drug therapy at an early stage. However, because patients often take multiple medications and the number of prescriptions is high, it is difficult for pharmaceutical staff to review every single prescription.  Given limited staffing resources, there is a need for a practical method to focus on the prescriptions and circumstances that are particularly prone to medication-related problems.
The aim of this study is to examine whether targeted validation of prescriptions based on risk-stratified filtering is as effective as reviewing all prescription lines. The study will investigate whether this approach can identify clinically relevant problems and opportunities for pharmaceutical intervention in drug therapy just as reliably. In the long term, the aim is to develop a strategy suitable for everyday use that supports safe and efficient medication management in the hospital.
conditions: Focusing available pharmaceutical personnel resources on clinically relevant issues
